method: The 30 pilot photos (with their original-subject comparison, as in a run) and 39 source-labelled lookalike photos (no subject prompt, as in #11) are cut into ranking revision 4 windows. Each pinned model's text tower embeds the fixed prompts once, as a server would for a device. Each image-tower artefact encodes every window in its own process on CPU with 4 threads and batches of up to 16, the first photo warmed up untimed. A candidate's window similarities are read like a run's and compared with the BioCLIP 2 fp32 reference against versioned thresholds. Size is the artefact on disk; peak memory is the encoding process's peak resident set; latency is image encoding only (pre-processing excluded).
caveats: Desktop CPU latency and memory are not phone latency or memory: phones differ in CPU, accelerators, runtime and thermal limits, and platform conversion (Core ML, TFLite, ExecuTorch) is deferred to the platform choice (#50). Parity means agreement with the reference on 69 source-labelled photos, not accuracy; the pilot has no independent background-plant labels (#12). A variant that keeps parity here can still diverge on photos unlike these.
command: uv run python scripts/compare_optimised.py --pilot-dir <scratch copy of data/pilot> --run nelson-tasman-3e62ad801459 --lookalikes <lookalike dir> --work <scratch dir> --output benchmarks/optimised-model-parity.json

why.max_margin_drift: Largest change in any photo's margin for any watchlist species. BioCLIP 2's only incidental candidate in the pilot sits at +0.009 and its weakest reference at +0.051, so 0.01 can move a photo that is already at the zero line but cannot push a validated reference to it.
why.unexplained_top_changes: Photos whose top suggestion changes although the reference's winning margin led the candidate's choice by more than twice the drift limit. If every margin moves by at most the drift limit, only such near-ties can swap.
why.references_lost: Reference photos (source-labelled watchlist weeds) that the reference ranks as their own weed with a positive margin but the candidate does not. Every pilot reference passes with both pinned models, so losing one is a regression.
why.lookalikes_newly_positive: Lookalike photos (native or other plants) that newly beat every comparison label as the weed they resemble. Rejecting lookalikes is why BioCLIP 2 became the default (#14), so an optimisation may not give any of that back.
why.incidental_queue_swaps: At each budget, photos in the reference's incidental review queue that the candidate replaces. One swap per budget is tolerated because most incidental margins are negative and close together; more means a reviewer would see a materially different queue.

conclusion: Kept parity: onnx-fp32, torch-fp16. Failed parity: onnx-int8, onnx-int8-per-channel, bioclip-vit-b16, bioclip-vit-b16-onnx-int8. Measured against thresholds version 1.
